To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
language evolution is a hot topic in computational linguistics and that the surveyed language evolution model are mostly based on evolutionary biology and cognitive science.

1) the most cited models are those based on the Baldwin effect and those that consider language as a complex adaptive system; 2) most of the models consider a small number of speakers (10-20) and the most used language is English; and 3) the most common validation techniques are simulations and mathematical analysis, while the most common comparison techniques are the analysis of the model dynamics and the analysis of the results.
language evolution models are mainly validated using simulations and that the most common approach for comparing the models is to use the same set of parameters.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What models have been proposed to model language evolution in the last decade and how have they been evaluated?

the following questions: What are the main models for language evolution in the new millennium? What is their scientific impact? What are the main strategies for validating and testing the models? How these strategies have been applied by different models?
the analysis of the evolution and dynamics of language and how it is modeled in the literature.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the modeling of language evolution is a very active and promising research field that will be able to provide a lot of new insights in the near future.

the field of language evolution modeling has been growing in terms of the number of publications and citations, and the number of models, but it still needs to be consolidated and matured to be considered a well-established scientific field.
the models reviewed in the present work have been developed to study the emergence, evolution and extinction of languages.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the models of language evolution have been mainly based on the evolution of lexicon, phonology and morphology, while the evolution of syntax and semantics has not been widely studied.
the models surveyed are not only a reflection of the evolution of language, but they are also an expression of the evolution of science itself.
the surveyed literature is characterized by the application of different strategies for modeling the evolution of language, but the validation and comparison of the models are usually not performed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the field of language evolution is currently dominated by the study of language emergence in artificial agents and that there is a lack of models of language evolution in human populations.

, despite the large number of models surveyed and the diversity of approaches and techniques used, the majority of them are not validated by empirical evidence and, consequently, their scientific impact is limited.
there is still a lot of work to be done to provide a complete picture of language evolution, but the research field is growing and it is likely to be more active in the near future.
